expectations.text: Claude identifies the density spike (more users clustering at 41-45 than expected) as a serious threat to the RDD — this pattern suggests score manipulation (gaming) near the threshold, not sampling noise
expectations.evidence: The response states: 'The spike in scores at 41–45 — more users clustering just above the threshold than a smooth distribution would predict — is the canonical signature of manipulation.' It frames this as a fundamental violation, not noise.

expectations.text: Claude explains WHY this matters for RDD: if users or CSMs can influence scores near the cutoff, users near the threshold are no longer as-good-as-randomly assigned to treatment/control, violating the local randomization assumption
expectations.evidence: The response explains: 'The entire logic of RDD rests on the idea that users just below 40 and just above 40 are effectively identical on all characteristics — observed and unobserved — except for treatment assignment. This near-randomness is what makes the comparison causal... If units can sort themselves to one side of the threshold, that near-randomness is gone.' It also includes a DAG showing how the confounder opens an unblocked fork.

expectations.text: Claude rejects the 'only communicated internally' argument as insufficient to rule out manipulation — internal staff (CSMs) knowing the cutoff is exactly the mechanism that enables strategic score inflation
expectations.evidence: The response directly addresses this: 'The claim is: the threshold was only communicated internally... This argument rules out possibility (1) above — user manipulation — but it does not rule out possibilities (2) or (3).' It then explains that support staff knowing the rule can sort users across the threshold.

expectations.text: Claude recommends a formal density test (McCrary test or equivalent) at the threshold and pre-treatment covariate balance checks near the cutoff as diagnostic steps before trusting the RDD estimate
expectations.evidence: The response recommends: 'Run the McCrary (2008) density test or Cattaneo-Jansson-Ma (2018) local polynomial density test' and 'Look at covariate balance across the threshold for pre-treatment variables that should be smooth (account age, industry, plan tier, prior support contacts).'
